resources.string: Refresh checks the server first. Applying your change creates a new attempt against its latest version. An earlier uncertain attempt may already have succeeded. Dropping this attempt removes only its local journal; it does not undo a server change.

The server vault identity changed. Discard this device’s old pending password and settings changes, then download the replacement vault. This does not reset or delete the server vault. Export a backup first if you need your local changes.
Choose an enabled destination. The original is removed only after the destination is verified. A stopped or uncertain move stays below for review.
This removes its encrypted recovery copy. It does not undo either store’s completed or pending changes. Verify both stores before continuing.
Use a separate passphrase to protect this portable backup. Passwords and notes are included. Account identities, server metadata and sign-in tokens are excluded. Keep the file and passphrase safe.
Import into the selected store. Existing different passwords are never overwritten. Entries are journaled before upload and remain available below if an import stops. Enter the backup passphrase.
The server vault changed. Review recovery before applying old changes.

This file contains visible passwords, usernames and default notes. Anyone with access to the chosen destination can read them. CSV does not preserve named notes, hidden-note settings or never-save rules; use the encrypted backup to retain those. Use CSV only with a password manager. Opening it in spreadsheet software can interpret credential text as formulas.

Import this Google Password Manager CSV into the selected store. Passwords and notes remain on this phone until you authorize upload by continuing. Existing different credentials are never overwritten. Each entry is journaled before upload so interrupted imports can be resumed below.
